title: Open WebUI folders -- T1485 shared-write collaborator deletes owner's chat subtree
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70494 (GHSA-3cg5-48j3-v4gv,
CVSS 8.1 HIGH), affecting Open WebUI from 0.10.0 until 0.11.0.

The `DELETE /api/v1/folders/{id}` handler
(`backend/open_webui/routers/folders.py`) allowed a user granted WRITE
access to a shared chat folder to permanently delete chats and messages
belonging to the folder OWNER -- not merely their own contribution. The
deletion cascade is correctly bound to the folder owner's id, but the
SUBFOLDER check accepted any inherited write grant instead of requiring
actual ownership or administrator status. A collaborator with nothing
more than write access can therefore destroy the owner's entire
subtree, or force-move chats out of it when `delete_contents=false`.

Detection logic flags a `DELETE /api/v1/folders/{id}` request whose
caller is NOT the folder's owner -- the endpoint's own authorization
gap is precisely this: any write-grant holder passes where only
ownership/admin should.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact router file and PR), fixed in 0.11.0.
